title: Salesforce consumer secret in a client_secret field or Basic envelope
summary: A synthetic consumer secret as the client_secret parameter of a form-encoded token request, in a raw request body and a curl data argument, and inside the encoded Basic credential of a token request.
rationale: Salesforce documents the client_secret parameter of the web server flow token request and an HTTP Basic form that carries client_id and client_secret in the Authorization header. The documentation states no prefix, alphabet or width, so the field name or the scheme is the only identifying context and no bare-value rule is implied. In a form body the extent stops at the next delimiter. In the Basic form the secret exists only inside the encoded credential, so the extent is the whole encoded token. The consumer key is public, and the signature member of a token response is derived output, not the secret.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the value of a client_secret parameter of a Salesforce token request, and the encoded credential after the Basic scheme, are treated as a credential. Salesforce documents the parameter and the Basic form (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and generic attribution are the project's decisions.
